# `kernel/UiSounds.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/UiSounds.js`

UiSounds.js — OS-wide UI sound engine (kernel service). Procedurally synthesizes short UI sounds (click, open, close, notify, error, …) through the OS AudioDriver's shared context, so every cue is mixed and volume- controlled centrally (it appears in the Sound mixer as a "System sounds" session). Sounds are auto-triggered from OS-wide kernel events (panel open/close/minimize/ restore, notifications, theme toggle) and from a global click listener, so the whole desktop gets feedback without each app wiring anything. Apps can also play a cue explicitly via syscalls.ui.sound('click'). ── Future customization ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Every cue is a named entry in a registry. A mod / sound pack can override or add cues at runtime: kernel.uiSounds.register('click', (ctx, out, t0) => { ... custom synth ... }); kernel.uiSounds.register('coin', (ctx, out, t0) => { ... new cue ... }); Per-cue enable flags, global enable, and volume persist in localStorage, ready for a settings UI (the Sound app exposes the global toggle + volume today).

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
